section_summary.extract_value: Abstract reports a single (unnamed) study using confirmatory factor analysis of a Cantonese translation of the Body Appreciation Scale among women (n = 1319) and men (n = 1084) in Hong Kong. A modified two-dimensional structure retaining 9 of 13 BAS items had the best fit, but only the General Body Appreciation factor showed adequate internal consistency and construct validity, including significant correlations with BMI and self-esteem (and among women, actual-ideal weight discrepancy). No mention of 'Study 1' or multiple separately labeled studies is present.
section_summary.evidence_source: Previous research has suggested that the factor structure of Body Appreciation Scale (BAS), a widely-used measure of positive body image, may not be cross-culturally equivalent. Here, we used confirmatory factor analysis to evaluate the conceptual equivalence of a Chinese (Cantonese) translation of the BAS among women (n = 1319) and men (n = 1084) in Hong Kong. Instead, a modified two-dimensional structure, which retained 9 of the 13 BAS items in two factors, had the best fit. This factor also had good patterns of construct validity, as indicated through significant correlations with participant body mass index, self-esteem, and (among women) actual-ideal weight discrepancy.
